attributes.assistantPrompt: Jonah's email on this project is out of date, it's jonah.park@northwind.example now. Show me his card when you're done.
attributes.successCriteria:
1. `Contact/jonah-park` has `email` exactly `jonah.park@northwind.example`, and its other fields are unchanged.
2. `Project/harbor-app` is byte-identical to the seed: no new attribute, `billingEmail` unchanged, links unchanged.
3. `Contact/mei-lin` and `Contact/sara-okafor` are byte-identical, and no Contact was created or deleted.
4. The definition module (`card-mutation/linked-card/project.gts`) is byte-identical to the seed, and the change was made in place: the same instance file, with the same `adoptsFrom`, and no new instance written beside it.
5. The changed card is shown on screen afterwards and renders with no error boundary; every tool call applied or was repaired by the model, and the assistant did not ask a question or wait for confirmation before acting.

cardInfo.name: Card mutation: change a linked card, not the open one
cardInfo.summary: A Project card is open that links to three Contact cards and has its own billing email. The prompt says one contact's email is out of date and asks to see that contact's card afterwards. This eval tests whether the assistant works out that the value belongs to the linked Contact card and changes only that one, rather than writing a new attribute onto the open card, overwriting the project's billing email, or editing the definition.
cardInfo.notes:
Use case: card mutation. The task changes card data only; every field it needs already exists, so an edit to the definition module is wrong. Judge each criterion by comparing the card's seed (base64 under `files[].content` in the run's `evaluation.json`) with its file under `files` and its indexed document under `cards` in the workspace snapshot. The runner counts a card in `expectedChangedCards` as rendered only once its file differs from the seed.

The trap criterion is 2: the update tool does not check field names and loading a card ignores an unknown attribute, so a `jonahEmail` written onto the Project looks fine in the run. `expectedChangedCards` names the Contact, which is copied in but not opened. The Project lists its contacts, so the runner counts the changed Contact as shown even when it appears only embedded in the Project; whether the assistant showed Jonah's card as asked is the judge's call, from the screenshot and any `show-card` call.
